title: Path traversal on the WRITE side: join/resolve semantics let input escape the base dir
index_line: T-0006 · FILE_WRITE · write flavor first (RCE-adjacent) · join-reset semantics per language · corroborated
invariant_violated: The app believes a joined path stays under its base directory; join/resolve semantics let an absolute or dot-dot component escape it.

mechanism.does: attacker controls a path-ish component (filename, entry name, storage key, script name)
component joined/concatenated onto a base directory
guard defeated: non-recursive replace('../'), basename-only checks, decode-after-check — or resets make the guard moot (absolute input replaces the base)
file written (or read) outside the base — write flavor: overwrite startup scripts, .bashrc, a required module, authorized_keys, cron

source.http.request.value: path-ish input: name, key, entry.name, template/scaffold names

fs.path.join.value: the join primitive — reset semantics differ per language and decide the payload

guard.resolve-check.value: the correct guard is resolve-then-prefix-check on the DECODED value; look for it done on the raw value, before decoding, or not at all

encoding.path.value: ../../../ · %2e%2e%2f · %252e (double) · overlong UTF-8 · ..\ · absolute '/etc/cron.d/x' on reset-primitive languages

preconditions.expr: varies — upload/download features usually authenticated user

success: write lands outside the base dir (sandbox PoC: marker file in a known out-of-tree location)
archive member resolves outside the extraction dir (zip-slip/symlink)
failure_like: resolve-then-prefix check present and applied to the decoded value — path stays under base
basename() strips traversal before the join
false_positive: join primitive does not reset AND the resolved path is re-checked — correctly guarded, not a finding

hazards: reset semantics per language are load-bearing: python/dotnet/java-resolve/rust REPLACE on absolute — no dotdot needed there; node join does NOT (its reset primitive is resolve)
Windows adds ..\ and drive-absolute forms — test both separators
non_transfers: object stores keyed without filesystem semantics
